sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: If you've listened to the show for a while, you know that we're big fans of icons and symbols and signage.
sentences.zh: 如果你收听这个节目一段时间了，你就会知道我们非常喜欢图标、符号和标牌。

sentences.en: And one of the main places you encounter those is on the road.
sentences.zh: 而你遇到这些东西的主要场所之一就是在路上。

sentences.en: So in our ongoing ubiquitous icon series, we're taken to the highways.
sentences.zh: 所以在我们持续进行的无处不在的图标系列中，我们将目光投向了公路。

sentences.en: I'm thinking we should call this one Highways 101, you know?
sentences.zh: 我想我们应该把这集叫做“101号公路”，你觉得呢？

sentences.en: I like it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢。

sentences.en: I like it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢。

sentences.en: Highways 101.
sentences.zh: 101号公路。

sentences.en: That's Kurt Kolstad.
sentences.zh: 那是柯特·科尔斯特ッド。

sentences.en: He's our digital director and co-author of the book, The 99% Invisible City.
sentences.zh: 他是我们的数字总监，也是《99%隐形城市》一书的合著者。

sentences.en: One of the things Kurt does is he checks our inbox for listener-submitted ideas, combs through all of them.
sentences.zh: 柯特的工作之一就是查看我们的收件箱，寻找听众提交的创意，并对所有这些创意进行梳理。

sentences.en: And earlier this summer, a 99PI fan named Daniel wrote us about a strange stop sign that he encountered while traveling.
sentences.zh: 今年夏天早些时候，一位名叫丹尼尔的99PI粉丝写信给我们，讲述了他在旅行中遇到的一个奇怪的停车标志。

sentences.en: And you started digging into this story.
sentences.zh: 然后你开始深入挖掘这个故事。

sentences.en: Yeah, so his email started like this.
sentences.zh: 是的，他的电子邮件是这样开头的。

sentences.en: A couple of years ago, we took a trip to Hawaii and my wife became obsessed over a few blue stop signs we saw in parking lots.
sentences.zh: 几年前，我们去夏威夷旅行，我妻子对我们在停车场看到的几个蓝色停车标志着迷了。

sentences.en: The signs were the size and shape and used the same lettering as normal red stop signs, but they were bright blue.
sentences.zh: 这些标志的大小、形状以及使用的字体都与正常的红色停车标志相同，但它们是亮蓝色的。

sentences.en: So I don't think I've ever seen that before.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我以前从来没有见过这个。

sentences.en: I had never seen this either, either in images or in real life.
sentences.zh: 我也从未见过，无论是在图片中还是在现实生活中。

sentences.en: So I started looking into why some were blue, and that turned out to be pretty easy to figure out.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始调查为什么有些是蓝色的，结果发现这很容易弄清楚。

sentences.en: But it got me wondering something a lot more fundamental, which is, why are the rest of them all red, right?
sentences.zh: 但这让我开始思考一个更基本的问题，那就是，为什么其余的标志全都是红色的，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Why is that such a thing in the first place?
sentences.zh: 为什么一开始会有这种现象？

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah, and that got me into, of course, digging into the whole history of stop signs.
sentences.zh: 是的，这自然而然地让我开始深入研究停车标志的整个历史。

sentences.en: Of course, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，当然。

sentences.en: That's the only way this is going to go with you.
sentences.zh: 跟你在一起，事情只能这样发展。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's just my nature.
sentences.zh: 是的，这只是我的天性。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And as I was looking into this, this one figure kept popping up everywhere I looked, a guy named William Phelps Eno,
sentences.zh: 当我研究这个时，有一个人物在我寻找的每个地方不断出现，一个名叫威廉·菲尔普斯·埃诺的人，

sentences.en: who in the early 1900s became known as the father of traffic safety.
sentences.zh: 他在20世纪初被称为交通安全之父。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧。

sentences.en: So what do you have to do to earn that title, the father of traffic safety?
sentences.zh: 那么，你需要做什么才能赢得“交通安全之父”这个称号？

sentences.en: So Eno was born way back in the 1850s.
sentences.zh: 所以埃诺出生于遥远的19世纪50年代。

sentences.en: And if you think about it, you know, 1850s, he's in New York.
sentences.zh: 如果你想想看，你知道的，19世纪50年代，他在纽约。

sentences.en: This is a New York without cars.
sentences.zh: 这是一个没有汽车的纽约。

sentences.en: So, of course, it's a New York without stop signs.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，这是一个没有停车标志的纽约。

sentences.en: Without stop signs.
sentences.zh: 没有停车标志。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The roads back then were kind of this open space that was shared by carriages and pedestrians, and they moved all around.
sentences.zh: 那时的道路有点像一个开放的空间，由马车和行人共享，他们到处移动。

sentences.en: It was a lot different.
sentences.zh: 那有很大不同。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: And there was, like, some attempts to do some traffic management and stuff, but it was all kind of ad hoc and, like, you know, people standing in the street,
sentences.zh: 当时有一些进行交通管理之类的尝试，但都是临时的，比如，你知道的，有人站在街上，

sentences.en: and it wasn't very organized.
sentences.zh: 而且它不是很系统化。

sentences.en: It all got worse, right?
sentences.zh: 情况变得更糟了，对吧？

sentences.en: As more technologies evolved and more and more people were on the streets and, you know, cars started showing up.
sentences.zh: 随着越来越多的技术发展，街上的人越来越多，你知道的，汽车开始出现。

sentences.en: And it just was increasingly clear that this was a mess and it was going to need some kind of regulation.
sentences.zh: 而且越来越清楚的是，这是一团糟，需要某种形式的监管。

sentences.en: And so was Eno some kind of road expert?
sentences.zh: 那么埃诺是什么道路专家吗？

sentences.en: Is that what he was working on?
sentences.zh: 这就是他一直在研究的吗？

sentences.en: Well, that's the thing.
sentences.zh: 这就是关键所在。

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 并不是。

sentences.en: He came from this family real estate business, decided it wasn't for him.
sentences.zh: 他来自一个家族房地产企业，决定那不适合他。

sentences.en: It wasn't his passion.
sentences.zh: 那不是他的热情所在。

sentences.en: His passion was traffic.
sentences.zh: 他的热情是交通。

sentences.en: So in 1900, he writes this article, and it's not entirely clear in hindsight if he realized what he was doing at the time,
sentences.zh: 所以在1900年，他写了一篇文章，事后来看，并不完全清楚他当时是否意识到自己在做什么，

sentences.en: but he basically was writing a treatise that would lay the groundwork for everything he would do for the rest of his life.
sentences.zh: 但他基本上是在写一篇论文，为他余生所做的一切奠定基础。

sentences.en: So in the end, he would come around to, you know, inventing and evolving all different kinds of traffic innovations, things we take for granted today,
sentences.zh: 因此，最终他会发明并发展各种各样的交通创新，这些都是我们今天认为理所当然的事情，

sentences.en: like rotary junctions and pedestrian crossing.
sentences.zh: 比如环形交叉路口和人行横道。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So he really earned that title, the father of traffic safety.
sentences.zh: 所以他真的是实至名归地获得了“交通安全之父”的称号。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: And once his ideas got some traction in the US, he began helping other cities create traffic plans and some really recognizable designs traced back to him,
sentences.zh: 一旦他的想法在美国获得了一些关注，他便开始帮助其他城市制定交通规划，一些真正易于识别的设计都可以追溯到他，

sentences.en: like roundabouts at Piccadilly Circus in London and around the Arc de Triomphe in Paris.
sentences.zh: 比如伦敦皮卡迪利圆环和巴黎凯旋门周围的环岛。

sentences.en: And he was even inducted into the Legion of Honor by the French government after World War I.
sentences.zh: 甚至在第一次世界大战后，他还被法国政府授予荣誉军团勋章。

sentences.en: For traffic?
sentences.zh: 因为交通？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Like that's what he got that?
sentences.zh: 就因为这个他得到了那个？

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: He essentially got, you know, France's equivalent of a knighthood for traffic design.
sentences.zh: 他基本上获得了法国相当于爵士头衔的交通设计奖。

sentences.en: But if you think about it from their perspective, his traffic designs helped get French troops to the front lines, which in turn helped them hold off the Germans during the war.
sentences.zh: 但如果你从他们的角度来想，他的交通设计帮助法国军队到达前线，这反过来又帮助他们在战争期间抵挡住了德国人。

sentences.en: France is pushing like 60,000 troops towards Verdun to halt the German advance towards Paris.
sentences.zh: 法国正将大约6万名士兵推向凡尔登，以阻止德国人向巴黎推进。

sentences.en: It was all made possible by this guy's traffic planning.
sentences.zh: 这一切都得益于这家伙的交通规划。

sentences.en: And so was Eno the man who invented the stop sign?
sentences.zh: 那么埃诺是发明停车标志的人吗？

sentences.en: Well, that's the thing.
sentences.zh: 这就是关键所在。

sentences.en: I kind of fell down this rabbit hole looking into him.
sentences.zh: 我在研究他时，有点陷入了这个兔子洞。

sentences.en: But one thing I realized along the way was that I was never going to find the inventor of the stop sign because it's one of those things that has existed in various forms for a while now.
sentences.zh: 但我在过程中意识到的一点是，我永远不可能找到停车标志的发明者，因为这是那种以各种形式存在了一段时间的东西。

sentences.en: But it's safe to say that Eno played a really big role in popularizing stop signs and yield signs and that kind of signage infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定地说，埃诺在普及停车标志、让行标志以及这类标牌基础设施方面发挥了非常大的作用。

sentences.en: And that's why his name comes up so much when you're looking into these things.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你在调查这些事情时，他的名字会如此频繁地出现。

sentences.en: And also, you know, put this in context, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，把这放在背景中看，对吧？

sentences.en: Stop signs back then, they weren't what we think of as stop signs today.
sentences.zh: 那时的停车标志，并不是我们今天所认为的停车标志。

sentences.en: Their designs varied from place to place.
sentences.zh: 它们的设计因地而异。

sentences.en: One of the first ones that popped up in Detroit in, I think it was 1915, had black lettering on a white background, presumably for contraSt.
sentences.zh: 最早出现在底特律的标志之一，我想是在1915年，是在白色背景上有黑色字母，大概是为了形成对比。

sentences.en: So they really, they came in all these different shapes and sizes and there was no sort of one person you could say, aha, that guy made the stop sign.
sentences.zh: 所以它们确实有各种不同的形状和大小，没有哪一个人可以说是，啊哈，那个人制作了停车标志。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I think that makes sense to me that there would be a need for stop signs and therefore they would be invented in multiple places and multiple times.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我认为对我来说这合情合理，因为会有对停车标志的需求，因此它们会在多个地方、多个时间被发明出来。

sentences.en: So when did they sort of get this octagonal shape that we attribute to them?
sentences.zh: 那么它们是什么时候获得了我们赋予它们的这种八角形形状的呢？

sentences.en: Like when did that happen?
sentences.zh: 这大概是什么时候发生的？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So that one actually does have a specific answer.
sentences.zh: 所以那个实际上有一个具体的答案。

sentences.en: And the answer is 1923.
sentences.zh: 答案是1923年。

sentences.en: That's when the Mississippi Valley Association of State Highway Departments decided to standardize the shape.
sentences.zh: 那是密西西比河谷州立公路部门协会决定将形状标准化的时间。

sentences.en: That's a very specific answer.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常具体的答案。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it was a pretty good idea to make it a non-standard shape, something that would stand out.
sentences.zh: 把形状做成非标准形状，也就是那种能脱颖而出的形状，真是个好主意。

sentences.en: But there was actually more to it than that.
sentences.zh: 但实际上还有更多的原因。

sentences.en: They had this idea that they could create an association between geometry and safety.
sentences.zh: 他们当时有一个想法，就是可以在几何形状和安全之间建立一种联系。

sentences.en: Explain more what you mean there.
sentences.zh: 请多解释一下你这话的意思。

sentences.en: Well, they believed that the shape itself could communicate something.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们相信形状本身可以传达一些东西。

sentences.en: Like part of what the sign was trying to do could be achieved through the shape of that sign.
sentences.zh: 就像标志试图实现的一部分功能可以通过该标志的形状来达到一样。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So we're not talking about just associating a rare shape with a specific meaning.
sentences.zh: 所以我们讨论的不只是将一个罕见的形状与一个特定的含义联系起来。

sentences.en: They actually, there's some kind of theory behind eight having a meaning that ties to stopping.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上，在“数字八”具有与停车相关的含义背后，存在着某种理论。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this was a huge surprise to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说是个巨大的惊喜。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because it sounds like nonsense.
sentences.zh: 因为听起来像无稽之谈。

sentences.en: It sounds right.
sentences.zh: 听起来挺对的。

sentences.en: It sounds sort of occult almoSt.
sentences.zh: 听起来几乎有点神秘主义。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: But I found it, I found this out through this New York Times Magazine article by Hilary Greenbaum and Dieter Rubenstein.
sentences.zh: 但我发现它是通过希拉里·格林鲍姆和迪特·鲁宾斯坦在《纽约时报杂志》上的一篇文章了解到的。

sentences.en: And I'm just going to have you read this excerpt for context that explains why the Highway Departments Association recommended different shapes for different signs.
sentences.zh: 我打算让你读一下这段摘录作为背景，它解释了公路部门协会为什么建议对不同的标志采用不同的形状。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Here it is.
sentences.zh: 在这里。

sentences.en: Quote, the recommendations were based on a simple, albeit not exactly intuitive idea.
sentences.zh: “引用，这些建议基于一个简单的、尽管并不完全直观的想法。

sentences.en: The more sides a sign has, the higher the danger level it invokes.
sentences.zh: 标志的边越多，它唤起的危险等级就越高。

sentences.en: By the engineer's reckoning, the circle, which has an infinite number of sides, screamed danger and was recommended for railroad crossings.
sentences.zh: 根据工程师的计算，有无限多条边的圆形尖叫着危险，被推荐用于铁路交叉口。

sentences.en: The octagon, with its eight sides, was used to denote the second highest level.
sentences.zh: 八角形有八条边，用于表示第二高的级别。

sentences.en: The diamond shape was for warning signs, and the rectangle and square shapes were used for informational signs.
sentences.zh: 菱形用于警告标志，矩形和正方形用于信息标志。

sentences.en: End quote.
sentences.zh: 引文结束。”

sentences.en: That is just wild.
sentences.zh: 这实在是太疯狂了。

sentences.en: It really is, right?
sentences.zh: 确实如此，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, there's so many things that I have, so many questions I have about this, and one of which is like, does a circle really have an infinite number of sides?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，关于这个我有太多的事情，有太多的问题，其中之一就是，圆形真的有无限多条边吗？

sentences.en: Well, yeah, so I'm thinking back to like, you know, grade school geometry, and I'm like, I think that there's something to that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，所以我想起了小学几何，然后我觉得，这其中有一定道理。

sentences.en: I think it's like.
sentences.zh: 我想它就像是。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, if you take the tangent of each point, and therefore it has an infinite number of sides.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，如果你取每个点的切线，因此它就有无限多条边。

sentences.en: But I don't think people perceive it as having infinite number of sides.
sentences.zh: 但我不认为人们认为它有无限多条边。

sentences.en: I think they perceive it as having one sign.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们认为它只有一个边。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's not like we look at a circle, a square, and a triangle, and we say, aha, right.
sentences.zh: 我们看圆形、正方形和三角形时，并不是说，啊哈，对吧。

sentences.en: Three, four, and infinite.
sentences.zh: 三、四和无限。

sentences.en: Infinite sign.
sentences.zh: 无限的标志。

sentences.en: It never in a million years occurred to me that there was some grand geometric theory behind U.S.
sentences.zh: 我有一百万年都不会想到美国停车标志形状背后有什么宏大的几何理论。

sentences.en: stop sign shapes.
sentences.zh: 但是如果你仔细想想，如果你开始剖析它，看看你周围的标志，你就能大致明白他们的意思，对吧？

sentences.en: But if you think about it, if you start to unpack it, and you look at signs around you, you can sort of understand what they're getting at, right?
sentences.zh: 就像，嗯，是的，矩形标志通常告诉你该走哪个出口之类的。

sentences.en: It's like, well, yeah, rectangular signs often tell you like what exit to take or something.
sentences.zh: 铁路交叉口有圆形，当然。

sentences.en: There's circles at railroad crossings, sure.
sentences.zh: 是的，但铁路交叉口也有栏杆，你知道的，因为有时候圆形还不够。

sentences.en: Yeah, but there's also like arm bars at railroad crossings, you know, like because the circle is not quite enough sometimes.
sentences.zh: 还有X形、栏杆和各种其他东西。

sentences.en: There's also Xs and arm bars and all kinds of other things.
sentences.zh: 所以我明白这背后有一种理论。

sentences.en: So I get that there's a theory behind it.
sentences.zh: 如果它在符号学上有某种基础的话，我愿意接受这种观点。

sentences.en: And if it has some kind of basis in semiotics, I'm willing to entertain that notion.
sentences.zh: 所以既然，你知道，1923年在密西西比，他们确定了形状。

sentences.en: So now that, you know, in 1923 in Mississippi, they established the shape.
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么想出红色背景的？

sentences.en: How did they come up with the red background?
sentences.zh: 嗯，那可能看起来是一个更简单的决定。

sentences.en: Well, that might seem like the simpler decision.
sentences.zh: 那个实际上花了更长的时间。

sentences.en: That one actually took a while longer.
sentences.zh: 当时，黄色经常被使用，部分原因只是材料科学的原因。

sentences.en: At the time, yellow was often used in part just for material science reasons.
sentences.zh: 比如他们无法获得真正具有高反射性且持久的红色。

sentences.en: Like they couldn't get a really good reflective durable red.
sentences.zh: 所以黄色在夜间显现出来。

sentences.en: And so yellow showed up at night.
sentences.zh: 因此黄色在夜间显现出来。

sentences.en: So for decades, that was the general standard.
sentences.zh: 所以几十年来，这一直是普遍的标准。

sentences.en: And then in the 1950s, they made red the official standard.
sentences.zh: 然后在20世纪50年代，他们将红色定为官方标准。

sentences.en: OK, so yellow, because you can make kind of a matte yellow and it contrasts really well with with black, for example, and it looks really good at night.

sentences.zh: 所以他就会开始刨开道路，尝试不同的设计。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He was perfectly suited to doing this.
sentences.zh: 他非常适合做这件事。

sentences.en: Just not quite legally allowed.
sentences.zh: 只是不太合乎法律允许。

sentences.en: But even then, he had another problem, too, which is that once he got this design together, he couldn't seem to find buyers until the Second World War came along.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，他也遇到了另一个问题，那就是当他把这个设计拼凑好后，似乎一直找不到买家，直到第二次世界大战爆发。

sentences.en: And suddenly there are wartime blackouts because of air raids.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，由于空袭，战时灯火管制开始了。

sentences.en: So nights are darker than ever.
sentences.zh: 所以夜晚比以往任何时候都要黑暗。

sentences.en: Drivers have been instructed to add dimmers to their headlamps and do other things to reduce their visibility on the road.
sentences.zh: 司机们被指示在车头灯上加装调光器并采取其他措施，以降低他们在路上的能见度。

sentences.en: And so accidents are happening and the government responds at first by painting white lines on the roads and on posts to help people see at night.
sentences.zh: 因此事故不断发生，政府最初的反应是在道路和柱子上刷上白线，以帮助人们在夜间看清路况。

sentences.en: And then, you know, suddenly Percy, who's been asking to get an audience with the government to see if they're interested, has these cat's eyes that are just perfect.
sentences.zh: 然后，你懂的，一直请求与政府会面以了解他们是否感兴趣的珀西，突然拥有了堪称完美的“猫眼”。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They use the illumination from cars to light up so they don't have like an independent source of light that would attract attention from the skies.
sentences.zh: 它们利用汽车的照明来发光，因此它们不需要像会吸引空中注意的独立光源那样。

sentences.en: And the next thing you know, the government is buying like 40,000 of these things a week.
sentences.zh: 接下来你知道的，政府每周要买大约4万个这东西。

sentences.en: And to some extent, I mean, this is where the design spread internationally.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，我的意思是，这就是这种设计向国际传播的途径。

sentences.en: So, you know, the other places, they also came up with their own and different solutions to fit their regional needs.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，其他地方也想出了他们自己的不同解决方案来适应各自的区域需求。

sentences.en: Like here in California, which is a huge state and there are lots of climate ranges.
sentences.zh: 比如在加利福尼亚，这是一个很大的州，有许多不同的气候带。

sentences.en: There's like hot and sunny places.
sentences.zh: 这里有炎热晴朗的地方。

sentences.en: There's cold and snowy places.
sentences.zh: 也有寒冷多雪的地方。

sentences.en: You need to use different markers in different places in different times.
sentences.zh: 你需要在不同的地方、不同的时间使用不同的路标。

sentences.en: And some reflectors are, you know, recessed into mountain roads, for example, so they don't get scraped up by plows.
sentences.zh: 例如，有些反光镜被嵌入山路中，这样就不会被除雪机刮坏。

sentences.en: You know, so there's lots of things you have to work on.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，所以有很多事情你需要去处理。

sentences.en: And so these things have been iterated and have different origins depending on where you are in the world.
sentences.zh: 因此，根据你身处世界何地，这些东西一直在改进并有着不同的起源。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And if you think about Percy's cat's eyes, too, you know, that was one of the things that made them work so well in Britain.
sentences.zh: 如果你想想珀西的“猫眼”，你知道的，这也是它们在英国如此奏效的原因之一。

sentences.en: It's like Britain is foggy and rainy.
sentences.zh: 就像英国又多雾又多雨。

sentences.en: And so these wipers were particularly useful.
sentences.zh: 所以这些刮水器特别有用。

sentences.en: So in a way, they were sort of, you know, they could be universal, but they also were very site specific as a solution.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，它们可以说是通用的，但作为一种解决方案，它们也非常具有特定地点针对性。

sentences.en: But no matter where you go, there is this there is this type that's more common than any other.
sentences.zh: 但无论你走到哪里，都有这样一种比任何其他类型都更常见的类型。

sentences.en: And it's basically just a trapezoid.
sentences.zh: 它基本上就是一个梯形。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's got a ramp up on one side, sort of flat top and then a ramp down on the other side.
sentences.zh: 它的一侧有坡道向上，顶部较为平坦，另一侧有坡道向下。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So you can see it in the two different directions, depending on which way you're going down the road.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以从两个不同的方向看到它，这取决于你走的是哪条路。

sentences.en: And it's not just the trapezoid shape that's used in a lot of different places.
sentences.zh: 不仅在许多不同地方使用梯形形状。

sentences.en: A lot of the colors are pretty common, too.
sentences.zh: 许多颜色也相当普遍。

sentences.en: So here in the U.S., for example, it's really common to have white reflectors to divide lanes and yellow reflectors on the edge of the road.
sentences.zh: 所以在美国，例如，通常用白色反光镜来划分车道，用黄色反光镜在路边。

sentences.en: But also there's some variations there, too.
sentences.zh: 但那里也有一些变化。

sentences.en: So like you can have greens and blues.
sentences.zh: 比如你可以有绿色和蓝色。

sentences.en: They indicate things, you know, that are on the side of the road.
sentences.zh: 它们指示路边的一些东西。

sentences.en: So pull off stops for cops can have a different color and like locations for fire hydrants to signal firefighters are also a different color.
sentences.zh: 因此，警察可以停靠的地点可以有不同的颜色，向消防员发出信号的消防栓位置也是不同的颜色。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I love the fact that you don't typically notice the color differences like you see the reflectors,
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这样一个事实，即你通常不会注意到颜色的差异，就像你看到反光镜一样，

sentences.en: but some of them are like queued in to tell different groups about what they can find.
sentences.zh: 但其中一些是有提示的，可以告诉不同的人他们能找到什么。

sentences.en: And then there's this other neat function that they can serve, too.
sentences.zh: 然后它们还能发挥另一个整洁的功能。

sentences.en: Because of their trapezoidal shape, they can have different colors facing different directions.
sentences.zh: 由于它们的梯形形状，它们可以面向不同的方向呈现不同的颜色。

sentences.en: So, for example, a reflector can have white on one side and that tells you, you know, you're going the right way.
sentences.zh: 例如，反光镜的一侧可以是白色的，这告诉你，你知道的，你走的是对的方向。

sentences.en: And then it can have red on the other side, which lets you know that you're going the wrong way.
sentences.zh: 然后另一侧可以是红色的，这让你知道你走错方向了。

sentences.en: Very much going the wrong way.
sentences.zh: 大错特错的方向。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It should probably just stop your car, maybe turn around slowly.
sentences.zh: 你可能应该直接停下车，也许慢慢调头。

sentences.en: If there's one lesson from this from this show, it's that if you see red, maybe stop.
sentences.zh: 如果从这个节目中能吸取到一个教训，那就是如果你看到红色，也许该停下来了。

sentences.en: Maybe stop.
sentences.zh: 也许该停下。

sentences.en: Consider stopping.
sentences.zh: 考虑停下。

sentences.en: Blue also sometimes, but not always.
sentences.zh: 有时蓝色也可以，但并非总是如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So in the book, we go over all these different details and we talk about different designs and we found in different places.
sentences.zh: 所以在书中，我们讨论了所有这些不同的细节，讨论了我们在不同地方发现的不同设计。

sentences.en: But, you know, we really tell the story through Percy Shaw.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我们主要是通过珀西·肖来讲述这个故事的。

sentences.en: And in the end, Percy became something of a local legend in Halifax.
sentences.zh: 最后，珀西成了哈利法克斯的一个当地传奇人物。

sentences.en: There's this plaque affixed to his old house and his design won a bunch of design awards.
sentences.zh: 他的老房子上贴着一块牌匾，他的设计赢得了许多设计奖项。

sentences.en: But he never really seemed to care about all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 但他似乎从来不在乎所有这些东西。

sentences.en: And he did travel for work, but he preferred to mostly stay close to home.
sentences.zh: 他的确为了工作而出差，但他更喜欢大部分时间呆在离家近的地方。

sentences.en: And one of the few ways that you can actually tell he'd become this kind of rich and influential guy was this Rolls Royce Phantom.
sentences.zh: 你可以真正看出他成为了这种富有且有影响力的人的少数几种标志之一，就是这辆劳斯莱斯幻影。

sentences.en: And people would tell stories about him, you know, riding around in it, driven by his chauffeur and often just traveling to and from his favorite pub.
sentences.zh: 人们会讲述关于他的故事，你知道的，他坐在车里，由他的司机驾驶，经常只是往返于他最喜欢的酒吧。

sentences.en: Along those very same roads that inspired him to create this thing that made him famous in the first place.
sentences.zh: 沿着正是那些启发他创造出让他成名的东西的道路行驶。

sentences.en: So there you have it.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样。

sentences.en: That's just one story of over 100 that we have in the book.
sentences.zh: 这只是我们在书中的100多个故事中的一个。

sentences.en: And in the 99% Invisible City, we have illustrations of all these things, too, including Percy's cat's eyes and a variation called Bot's Dots,
sentences.zh: 在《9%隐形城市》（The 99% Invisible City）中，我们也有所有这些东西的插图，包括珀西的“猫眼”和一种被称为“博茨圆点”（Bot's Dots）的变体，

sentences.en: which are really common in California.
sentences.zh: 这在加利福尼亚非常普遍。

sentences.en: And those trapezoidal reflectors that we talked about as well.
sentences.zh: 还有我们讨论过的那些梯形反光镜。

sentences.en: And this is definitely the kind of story you can expect from the upcoming book in general.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是你对即将出版的新书所能期待的那种故事。

sentences.en: You know, like we talk about specific designs and places and characters and all the ideas and lessons and histories that are specific to a place,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像我们讨论特定的设计、地点和人物，以及特定于某个地点的所有想法、教训和历史，

sentences.en: but also have global implications and global meaning.
sentences.zh: 但也具有全球意义和全球含义。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And while you're waiting for your copy of said book, I've also been writing up a bunch of articles about how the book was made and been answering a lot of questions people have.
sentences.zh: 在你等待这本书的时候，我也一直在写一堆关于这本书是如何制作的文章，并一直在回答人们提出的许多问题。

sentences.en: And, you know, I've been gathering some some process materials from our illustrator, Patrick Vail, and our designer, Raphael Gironi.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我一直在收集我们插画师帕特里克·维尔（Patrick Vail）和设计师拉斐尔·吉罗尼（Raphael Gironi）的一些制作材料。

sentences.en: And so I've been assembling these into some some neat surprises and sort of behind the scenes pieces about how we made the book, because, of course, we're a design show.
sentences.zh: 所以我把这些整理成了一些很棒的惊喜和幕后花絮，关于我们是如何制作这本书的，因为当然，我们是一个设计节目。

sentences.en: So we're not only interested in talking about design in the book, but we're also interested in talking about the design of the book.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不仅有兴趣在书中谈论设计，我们也有兴趣谈论这本书的设计。

sentences.en: And some of the process, the iterations that Raphael went through when he was working on the cover, for example, are super fascinating.
sentences.zh: 拉斐尔在制作封面时经历的一些过程和迭代，例如，超级迷人。

sentences.en: I even forgot some of the different versions that he did and the pictures, the drawings.
sentences.zh: 我甚至忘记了他做的一些不同版本和图片、画作。

sentences.en: They're so cool.
sentences.zh: 它们太酷了。

sentences.en: You should definitely check them out.
sentences.zh: 你绝对应该去看看。

sentences.zh: 它们全都在 99pi.org。
